introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: The function $y(x)$ satisfies the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = f(x,y)$ where $f(x,y) = 2 + \dfrac{y}{x}$ and $y(1) = 1$.
incertitudes: Question 3(ii) : le sujet ne précise pas les ordonnées à utiliser ; ce sont celles obtenues en (i) (règle de Simpson à deux intervalles de pas 0,05). La valeur exacte (solution y = x(1 + 2 ln x)) est donnée dans le corrigé pour contrôle.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the formula $y_{r+1} \cong y_r + hf(x,y)$ with $h = 0.05$ to obtain an approximate value for $y(1.1)$, giving your answer correct to three decimal places. *[4 marks]*
Use Simpson's rule to estimate the value of $\displaystyle\int_1^{1.1} y\,dx$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the three ordinates found in part (i), $y(1)=1$, $y(1.05)\approx1.15$ and $y(1.1)\approx1.3048$, with two strips of width $h=0.05$. Simpson's rule gives

$$\int_1^{1.1} y\,dx \approx \frac{h}{3}\Big[y_0 + 4y_1 + y_2\Big] = \frac{0.05}{3}\Big[1 + 4(1.15) + 1.3048\Big] = \frac{0.05}{3}\times 6.9048$$

$$\int_1^{1.1} y\,dx \approx 0.1151 \approx 0.115.$$

*Check.* The equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{y}{x}=2$ has integrating factor $\dfrac1x$, so $\dfrac{y}{x} = 2\ln x + 1$ and $y = x(1+2\ln x)$. Then $\displaystyle\int_1^{1.1} y\,dx = \Big[x^2\ln x\Big]_1^{1.1} = 1.21\ln 1.1 \approx 0.1153$, which agrees with the estimate to three decimal places.
